en: Prosperity!
The Chapter on the Contemptuous Repudiation of the Glory of Selflessness.
What is gained by having acquired knowledge honored by kings?
What is gained by having attained wealth and power?
What is gained by having enjoyed a woman of beautiful form?
By whom his own self had not yet been directly realized. || 1.1 ||
What is the use of being adorned with armlets and the like,
or what is the use of being clothed in silken garments and such? Or what is the use of being satiated with delicious food and the like?
By whom his own self had not been directly realized. || 1.2 ||
What is gained by seeing various beautiful lands?
What is gained by nourishing one's circle of kinsmen?
What is gained when the suffering of poverty and the like has perished?
By whom his own self had not been directly realized. || 1.3 ||
What is the use of bathing at sacred fords such as Jahnujā and the like?
What follows from giving gifts eighteen times over?
What is the use of chanting mantras by the millions?
By whom his own self had not been directly realized.
What does it matter if one's lineage is well-adorned,
or what if the body is covered in ashes?
What does it matter if one wears rudrākṣa beads and the like?
By whom his own self had not been directly realized. || 1.5 ||
What is the use of satisfying the Brahmins with food, or of pleasing the gods with sacrifices?
What is the use of filling all the worlds with one's fame?
By whom his own self had not been directly realized. || 1.6 ||
The body has been afflicted by fasts—what of it?
Sons have been obtained from one's own wife—what of it?
Or perhaps breath-control has been mastered—what of it?
By whom his own self had not been directly realized.
What more is gained if the enemy is defeated in battle?
Or what more if one is surrounded by friends?
Or what more if perfections are attained through yogic practices?
By whom his own self had not been directly realized.
What is gained by crossing the ocean on foot?
Or what is gained by confining the wind in a jar?
Or what is gained by lifting Mount Meru with one's hand?
By whom his own self had not yet been directly realized.
If poison is drunk like milk, what of it? If fire is swallowed like parched grain, what of it?
If one has reached the sky as a bird, what of it?
By whom his own self had not been directly realized.
What is gained by properly binding the fires and other elements?
What then by piercing the finest metals directly? What is gained by applying ointments and such to recover a deposited treasure?
By whom his own self had not been directly realized.
What is gained by attaining the sovereignty of the earth?
What is gained by accumulating the sovereignty of the gods?
And what is gained by attaining the leadership of ascetics?
By whom his own self was not directly realized. || 1.12 ||
If everyone has been paralyzed by mantras, what is the use of arrows? Or if the target has already been pierced, what is the use of them?
And even if the knowledge of the right time has been obtained, what then?
By whom his own self had not been directly realized.
Has the elephant of desire been shattered? What of it?
Has the onset of anger been blunted? What of it?
Has the embrace of greed been abandoned? What of it?
By whom his own self had not been directly realized.
Has the darkness of delusion been ground away? What then has arisen on earth? Or has pride been crushed? What then has arisen? Or has the affliction of envy been closed up? What then has arisen?
By whom his own self had not been directly realized. || 1.15 ||
Has the world of Dhātṛ been conquered? What of it?
Has the world of Viṣṇu been beheld? What of it?
Has the world of Śambhu been subdued? What of it?
By whom one's own self had not been directly realized.
He in whose heart this constant and thorough revulsion toward the non-self and its splendors arises, he alone is a fit vessel for the direct realization of the Self. 1.17
But others, deluded by the confusion of the illusory error of the world, never attain the direct realization of their own self anywhere on earth. 1.18

Thus ends [the work] composed by the venerable Śrī Śaṅkara Bhagavat, the teacher of the wandering mendicants (paramahaṃsa-parivrājaka-ācārya) and the disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavat-pūjyapāda.
The chapter on the reproach of the glory of the non-self is complete.
The Chapter on the Repudiation of the Glory of the Non-Self.
